# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable and widely-supported environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# This prevents interactive prompts during package installation, which is essential for automated builds.
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install system dependencies
# - build-essential, git, cmake: Core tools for compiling C++ applications from source.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone over https).
# - openmpi-bin, libopenmpi-dev: The Open MPI runtime and development libraries, essential for enabling MPI support.
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    ca-certificates \
    cmake \
    git \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    openmpi-bin && \
    # Clean up apt cache to reduce image size
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments, especially relevant for Kubernetes
# This ensures MPI applications can run as the root user, which is the default in this Dockerfile.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
# Direct MPI to use the primary TCP network interface (typically eth0 in containers).
# This is crucial for inter-pod communication in a Kubernetes cluster.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
# Explicitly select the desired BTL (Byte Transfer Layer) components.
# Exclude components like 'openib' (InfiniBand) which are not present in standard cloud CPU instances.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl=self,tcp,vader
# Prevents a potential warning/error with shared memory mechanisms in some container runtimes.
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none

# Set a consistent working directory for the build process.
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the Kripke repository from the master branch, build it with MPI enabled,
# install the executable, and clean up all source and build files in a single layer.
# This approach minimizes final image size.
# FIX: Added --recurse-submodules to the git clone command. This is required to fetch
# the BLT (Building Large Toolkits) build system, which Kripke depends on.
RUN git clone --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git -b master && \
    cd Kripke && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake. MPI is enabled, and it's optimized for release.
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D ENABLE_MPI=ON \
      .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available processor cores to speed up the build.
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # Per instructions, copy the final executable to a system location on the PATH.
    # This makes the application directly runnable from any directory.
    cp bin/kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke.exe && \
    # Return to the parent directory and remove all source and build artifacts.
    cd / && \
    rm -rf /opt/Kripke

# Set the default working directory for when the container starts.
WORKDIR /root

# Define the default command to execute when the container is run.
# Displaying the help message is a good default to verify the application is installed correctly.
CMD ["kripke.exe", "--help"]

# MiniCluster manifest for running the Kripke benchmark on a single AWS CPU node.
# This configuration creates a single-pod Flux instance (size: 1) and runs the
# specified command across 4 tasks within that pod.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-mc-aws-cpu
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster. A size of 1 keeps the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. These tasks will be distributed across the pods defined by 'size'.
  tasks: 4

  # Defines the application container to run within the Flux cluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # The command to be executed by Flux. The Flux Operator automatically wraps this
      # with 'flux run -n <tasks>'.
      command: kripke
      # When false, the command is executed in a separate Kubernetes Job managed by the Flux Operator.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Ensures that the operator logs any potential issues or misconfigurations strictly.
    strict: true

  # If set to false, the MiniCluster pods and associated resources will not be
  # deleted after the job completes, allowing for post-run inspection.
  cleanup: false

# MiniCluster manifest for running the Kripke benchmark on a single AWS CPU node.
# This version corrects a previous error by specifying the processor decomposition
# to match the number of tasks requested.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name of the MiniCluster instance.
  name: kripke-mc-aws-cpu
  # The namespace where the MiniCluster will be deployed.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster. A size of 1 keeps the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run. This must match the processor decomposition in the command.
  tasks: 4

  # Defines the application container to run within the Flux cluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # FIX: Added the --procs argument to specify a processor decomposition (2x2x1) that
      # matches the 4 tasks requested in spec.tasks. This resolves the application's
      # assertion failure when running in parallel.
      command: kripke --procs 2,2,1
      # When false, the command is executed in a separate Kubernetes Job managed by the Flux Operator.
      launcher: false

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    # Ensures that the operator logs any potential issues or misconfigurations strictly.
    strict: true

  # If set to false, the MiniCluster pods and associated resources will not be
  # deleted after the job completes, allowing for post-run inspection.
  cleanup: false

# MiniCluster manifest updated to fix a "command not found" error.
# The executable name is corrected from 'kripke' to 'kripke.exe'.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-mc-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # If set to false, the MiniCluster resources are not deleted after job completion.
  cleanup: false
  # Defines the application container to run within the Flux cluster.
  containers:
  - # FIX: Corrected the executable name to 'kripke.exe'. The previous command 'kripke'
    # failed with exit code 127 ("No such file or directory") because the binary in
    # the container is named 'kripke.exe'.
    command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,4
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
    # When false, the command is executed in a separate Kubernetes Job managed by the Flux Operator.
    launcher: false
  # Flux-specific configuration to target ARM architecture.
  flux:
    # Specifies the architecture for the flux view container.
    arch: arm
    # Overrides the default flux view container to use an ARM-compatible image.
    container:
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-rocky:arm-9
  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true
  # Pod-level scheduling constraints to target a specific AWS Graviton instance.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: hpc7g.16xlarge
  # The number of pods for the MiniCluster. A size of 1 keeps the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1
  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  tasks: 64

# MiniCluster manifest corrected to use the proper executable name 'kripke.exe'.
# This resolves the previous "command not found" error and subsequent container termination.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-mc-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods for the MiniCluster. A size of 1 keeps the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  tasks: 48

  # Defines the application container to run within the Flux cluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # FIX: Corrected the command to use the executable 'kripke.exe'. The previous
      # attempt failed because the binary in the container is named 'kripke.exe',
      # not 'kripke', leading to a "command not found" error.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 4,4,3
      # When false, the command is executed in a separate Kubernetes Job managed by the Flux Operator.
      launcher: false

  # Pod-level scheduling constraints to target a specific AWS instance type.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # If set to false, the MiniCluster resources are not deleted after job completion.
  cleanup: false

# MiniCluster manifest with corrected MPI process decomposition.
# This version fixes an application-level assertion failure from Kripke.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-mc-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods for the MiniCluster. A size of 1 keeps the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  tasks: 48

  # Defines the application container to run within the Flux cluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # FIX: Corrected MPI process decomposition from '--procs 4,4,3' to '--procs 3,4,4'.
      # The application failed because the number of Z-dimension zones (default 16) must be
      # evenly divisible by the number of Z-dimension processes. The previous value of 3
      # caused an error (16 % 3 != 0). The new value of 4 is a valid divisor (16 % 4 == 0),
      # while the total number of tasks remains 48 (3*4*4=48).
      command: kripke.exe --procs 3,4,4
      # When false, the command is executed in a separate Kubernetes Job managed by the Flux Operator.
      launcher: false

  # Pod-level scheduling constraints to target a specific AWS instance type.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # If set to false, the MiniCluster resources are not deleted after job completion.
  cleanup: false

# MiniCluster manifest with an adjusted problem size to fix domain decomposition.
# This version resolves an application-level assertion failure by specifying
# a compatible zone grid for the given process layout.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: kripke-mc-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods for the MiniCluster. A size of 1 keeps the entire job on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks to run.
  tasks: 48

  # Defines the application container to run within the Flux cluster.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:kripke
      # FIX: Added '--zones 24,24,24' to fix a domain decomposition error. The previous run failed
      # because the default zone count (16) was not divisible by the process count in the
      # X-dimension (3). The new zone dimensions (24,24,24) are divisible by the
      # corresponding process grid dimensions (3,4,4), allowing the simulation to run correctly.
      command: kripke.exe --procs 3,4,4 --zones 24,24,24
      # When false, the command is executed in a separate Kubernetes Job managed by the Flux Operator.
      launcher: false

  # Pod-level scheduling constraints to target a specific AWS instance type.
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: c7a.12xlarge

  # Logging settings for the Flux Operator.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # If set to false, the MiniCluster resources are not deleted after job completion.
  cleanup: false

kind: MiniCluster
